title: Unauthenticated login attempts can temporarily block an account on a process
description: The login route increments an account-keyed counter before checking credentials. Five attempts for the same normalized email cause later requests for that email to receive 429 responses on that process until the 15-minute window expires, regardless of attempt source IP. An unauthenticated caller able to reach the same process could temporarily prevent the account from logging in. Source supports the per-process behavior, but this audit did not establish practical effect across Vercel instances or independently reproduce it.
claimed_root_cause: The process-local login throttle counts attempts by SHA-256 of the normalized account email before password verification and rejects at five for the 15-minute window.

trace.description: POST /login checks Origin and a static CSRF header before body validation and throttling.
Email is trimmed and lowercased before the account key is computed.
A hash of the normalized email forms an account key independent of the IP key.
The throttle runs before passwordLogin verifies credentials, so failed attempts increment the counter.

trace.scope: Account login availability on one process
trace.description: At the account limit, later attempts receive 429 until the counter window expires.

evidence.description: Each router instance stores counters in an in-memory Map.
Account hash key is separate from the IP key.
Reached limits throw a 429 rate-limit error before credential verification.
Test source describes the five-attempt account cap and expiry recovery; not executed in this audit.

blockers: Required OS-enforced sandbox unavailable, so the bounded dummy-account reproduction was not run.
Source cannot establish Vercel function instance reuse or routing; practical deployment scope is unknown.
The selected skill prohibits deployed endpoint probes.

validation_plan.local: When the required sandbox exists, run the focused auth throttle integration test with a verified disposable TEST_DATABASE_URL and dummy account; verify five failed attempts from distinct simulated IPs on one process cause a later valid request to return 429 with Retry-After, then verify expiry recovery using the injected clock. Start a fresh app instance and verify its counters are isolated. Do not use hosted services or real credentials.
